name: The Meatmen
label: Touch and Go
lede: A Michigan grade-school teacher printed a punk fanzine on the school copier at 3 a.m., started the dirtiest band in hardcore, and ended up with two members of Minor Threat in his backing band.

eras.title: A teacher with a copy machine
eras.text: Robert Vermeulen taught third and fifth grade in Williamston, Michigan. At night he was Tesco Vee, co-editor of Touch and Go, a Lansing punk zine that would turn into one of America's great independent labels, and singer of a band built to offend everyone.

years.h: Tesco Vee and Dave Stimson start the Touch and Go fanzine
years.p: High school classmates Tesco Vee and Dave Stimson launch Touch and Go in East Lansing. Vee, a grade-school teacher, runs it off on the school photocopier at 3 a.m.
years.xp: The zine ran 22 issues. In 2010 Bazillion Points collected all of it in a book of more than 500 pages.

years.h: The first Meatmen practice, in an East Lansing attic
years.p: Tesco Vee gathers high school friends in an attic in East Lansing. He later told Vice that punk's do-it-yourself idea made him realize he could get onstage too.

years.h: First Meatmen show: a Windsor tavern with a frying-pan bartender
years.p: The Meatmen's debut gig is at the Coronation Tavern in Windsor, Ontario. Tesco Vee remembers the bartender hitting customers with a frying pan.

years.h: Meatmen Stomp lands on Touch and Go's first record
years.p: Touch and Go becomes a label, with [[Necros|a8971728-0985-4b30-a209-142784e7c3b8]] bassist [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] helping. The Meatmen's Meatmen Stomp is on its Process of Elimination 7" sampler, next to [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]].

years.h: Tesco Vee slam-dances with Fear on Saturday Night Live
years.p: Tesco Vee is part of the hardcore crowd John Belushi brings to NBC for [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]]'s Halloween 1981 set, along with Detroit's [[John Brannon|a3418f6c-a8b1-4565-9836-b389b405510a]] and kids from D.C.

eras.title: Blüd Sausage and a riot on Cass Avenue
eras.text: The Meatmen's records were titled to get banned, and their shows landed in the same scenes as Minor Threat and Negative Approach. By 1983 Tesco Vee had lost his teaching job, handed Touch and Go to Corey Rusk and headed for Washington, D.C.

years.h: Blüd Sausage EP · Touch and Go
years.p: The Meatmen's first EP: seven songs of gross-out hardcore that became the studio side of the band's 1983 album.
years.xp: Trouser Press lists a second 1982 EP, Crippled Children Suck, also on Touch and Go; Wikipedia dates it 1983. Song titles like Camel Jockeys Suck and One Down Three to Go were written to offend and did.

years.h: The Meatmen on the Freezer Theater bill that ends in a riot
years.p: Metro Times puts The Meatmen on the bill with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] at Detroit's Freezer Theater. A parking-lot riot, broken windows and arrests close the venue for good.

years.h: Tesco Vee loses his teaching job and heads for D.C.
years.p: Tesco Vee told Razorcake he lost his Michigan teaching position in 1982. A visit to a D.C. show with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and [[Youth Brigade|7029a4cb-83bc-4e5e-8d94-af9caefc453c]] had already hooked him, and he moves to the Washington area.

years.src: Wikipedia: We're the Meatmen...and You Suck!!
years.h: We're the Meatmen...and You Suck!! · Touch and Go
years.p: Side one is the Blüd Sausage EP; the rest is The Meatmen live in New York City, including Meatmen Stomp and Mister Tapeworm. Sixteen tracks in all.
years.xp: The line-up was Tesco Vee with Rich and Greg Ramsey on guitars, Mike Achtenburg on bass and drummers credited as Mr. X and Berl Johnson. Some sources call it a compilation, others a live album; many fans count it as the debut.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · Chunklet
years.h: Tesco Vee hands Touch and Go to Corey and Lisa Rusk
years.p: When Tesco Vee leaves Michigan, Corey Rusk and his wife Lisa take over Touch and Go and later move it to Chicago. Vee told Chunklet he'd never have predicted how big it got.
years.xp: Under the Rusks the label signed [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]], [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]], [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]] and [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]], on handshake deals that split profits 50–50 with the bands.

eras.title: Minor Threat in evening gowns
eras.text: In D.C. the Meatmen became a supergroup of sorts: two Minor Threat guitarists and Negative Approach's bassist behind a singer in costume. The records moved to Homestead and Caroline, and the joke got bigger and louder.

years.h: Minor Threat's Lyle Preslar and Brian Baker join The Meatmen
years.p: After [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] ends, guitarists [[Lyle Preslar|c1b9b78e-691f-424d-8ce1-53c87c24d299]] and [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] become Tesco Vee's new D.C. Meatmen.

years.h: Graham McCulloch of Negative Approach takes the Meatmen bass
years.p: Detroit's [[Graham McCulloch|a9cb94ec-b297-44d5-9ea1-dbefe4b26c33]], ex-[[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]], joins on bass, tying Tesco Vee's old Michigan scene to his new D.C. band. He stays until 1988.
years.xp: The same year Trouser Press credits Tesco Vee with a solo EP, Dutch Hercules, made with Preslar and Baker.

years.h: War of the Superbikes, produced by Ian MacKaye · Homestead
years.p: The first D.C. Meatmen album, with Lyle Preslar and Brian Baker on guitars and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]], their old Minor Threat singer, producing.

years.h: Brian Baker quits The Meatmen over the stage costumes
years.p: According to Tesco Vee, Brian Baker left The Meatmen because he was sick of wearing ballerina costumes and evening gowns onstage. Baker's next band was [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]].
years.xp: James Cooper took over Baker's guitar spot for the next album, according to Trouser Press.

years.h: Rock 'n' Roll Juggernaut mocks metal · Caroline
years.p: The Meatmen take aim at heavy metal on Caroline Records. Tesco Vee told Razorcake the parody ended up unexpectedly popular with fans.

years.h: The Meatmen's farewell tour
years.p: The D.C. Meatmen call it quits after a 1988 farewell tour. Caroline releases the live We're the Meatmen...and You Still Suck!!! in 1989.

eras.title: Toilet Slave and a pope on a rope
eras.text: Tesco Vee couldn't stay retired. A third Meatmen line-up made three more records in the mid-nineties before he announced, again, that he was done.

years.h: Tesco Vee reforms The Meatmen
years.p: A new Meatmen line-up starts recording for Tesco Vee's Meatking label. Toilet Slave follows in 1994.

years.h: Pope on a Rope
years.p: The mid-nineties Meatmen's second album, followed in 1996 by War of the Superbikes II.

years.h: Tesco Vee quits music and writes Dinosaur
years.p: Tesco Vee stops performing in 1996. The same year he writes Dinosaur, a song about playing punk since 1979.

years.h: Tesco Vee moves back to Michigan
years.p: After seventeen years in the Washington, D.C. area, Tesco Vee returns to Michigan.

eras.title: Negative Approach brings him back
eras.text: A reissue, a Detroit show backed by Negative Approach and a push from his son put Tesco Vee back onstage in his fifties, with a band half his age.

years.h: Touch and Go reissues Blight, Tesco Vee's noise band
years.p: Blight, Tesco Vee's early-eighties side project with ex-members of Lansing's [[The Fix|75b206a3-acca-4a37-8e4d-c29fbb0cba22]], gets a Touch and Go reissue.

years.h: Tesco Vee sings a Meatmen set with Negative Approach
years.p: In Detroit, [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] backs Tesco Vee for a 30-minute set. Vee credits the show, and his son's encouragement, with bringing The Meatmen back.
years.xp: By late 2008 he had a new line-up of musicians in their twenties, some from the band Chapstik, and plans for a covers album. His son worked as the band's road manager for a couple of years.

years.h: Cover the Earth, The Meatmen's covers album
years.p: Named after the Sherwin-Williams paint slogan, the album covers Black Randy, Thin Lizzy, Jimmy Dean and ABBA.

years.h: Bazillion Points publishes the complete Touch and Go zine
years.p: Touch and Go: The Complete Hardcore Punk Zine '79–'83 collects every issue Tesco Vee and Dave Stimson made. Westword reported 8,000 copies sold.

years.h: Savage Sagas, first new Meatmen songs in twenty years
years.p: Released on Self Destructo Records. Tesco Vee told Vice a legacy punk band has to really bring it every night.

years.h: Tesco Vee opens a vintage toy shop in Lansing
years.p: Tesco Vee opens a Lansing store stocked from his collection of toys from the 1940s to the 1980s: puppets, coloring books, figurines, character dolls and model kits.
